title: Super-Level-Set Regression: Conditional Quantiles via Volume Minimization
claim: Directly optimized level-set boundaries capture complex, asymmetric, and disjoint conditional structures at the target coverage without density estimation.
layout: 2 side-by-side scatter panels, left-to-right; green contour overlays on test points
description: Two side-by-side 2D scatter plots show synthetic conditional distributions in y1 and y2 coordinates. Pale gray-green dots are test points. A bold dark-green closed contour, labeled SLS in a legend box at top right of each panel, outlines the predicted region. The left panel shows an asymmetric star-shaped density. The contour is a single curved band tracing the dense left part of the star, with sparse tails of points outside it. The right panel shows three disjoint modes: a long diagonal ellipse at upper left, a wavy blob at right, and a curved crescent at bottom. Each has its own contour, and a few outlier points sit outside. Light dashed gridlines and serif axis labels give a clean look. The eye goes first to the green outlines wrapped around the dense point clouds.
caption: SLS regression on synthetic 2D distributions, sampling from P𝑌|𝑋for fixed 𝑋. Left: A single flow-based Mahalanobis frontier capturing an asymmetric, star-shaped density. Target and empirical coverage are both 70%. Right: A union of four flow components seamlessly adapting to a disjoint, three-mode distribution. The model successfully allocates mass despite the structural mismatch of components to modes, achieving an exact empirical coverage of 90%.
abstract: Constructing minimum-volume prediction regions that satisfy conditional coverage is a fundamental challenge in multivariate regression. Standard approaches rely on explicitly estimating the full conditional density and subsequently thresholding it. This two-step plug-in process is notoriously difficult, sensitive to estimation errors, and computationally expensive. One would like to instead optimize the region directly. Formulating a direct solution is challenging, however, because it requires minimizing a volume objective that is coupled with the conditional quantiles of the model's own estimation error. In this work, we address this challenge. We introduce super-level-set regression (SLS), a novel mathematical framework that successfully resolves this implicit coupling, allowing us to directly parameterize and optimize the geometric boundaries of the target conditional level sets. By bypassing full distribution estimation and leveraging flexible volume-preserving frontier functions, our approach natively captures complex, multimodal, and disjoint conditional structures end-to-end. Ultimately, SLS offers a new perspective on multivariate conditional quantile regression, replacing the restrictive assumptions of density-first methods with a direct geometric optimization strategy.
